title: Regional shadow routing and rescue corridor for pinned model versions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Customers can pin a specific model version in a given region. When that exact version becomes unavailable (deprecation, incompatible weights, or capacity pressure), we need a predictable, observable, and low-risk way to route traffic to compatible alternatives while minimizing latency/regression risk and preserving contractual pin semantics.

This ticket proposes two related controls: (1) Regional Shadow Routing — a background warmup + scoring system that keeps a small fraction of traffic mirrored to fallback candidates in the same region to maintain KV cache and warm kernel paths; (2) Rescue Corridor — an emergency runtime policy that executes a deterministic, score-driven substitution path when a pinned model in a region fails or is retired.

Goals:
- Avoid cold-start/compatibility regressions when automatically substituting pinned versions.
- Minimize user-visible latency/regression while preserving pin expectations (transparent substitution with strong telemetry and notification).
- Provide operators clear signals and safe rollback/override controls via Console.

Non-Goals:
- Model policy for global cross-region migrations (out-of-scope; separate project).
- Replacing manual pinning process or policy approval flows — this augments runtime behavior only.
acceptance_criteria: Regional shadow routing implemented as a per-customer per-region mirror stream that can be toggled and throttled via config

Scoring function for fallback candidates implemented (components: semantic compatibility score, p95 latency delta, cost delta, warmness metric, and regional locality), and scores are published to model catalog

Rescue Corridor executes deterministic substitution when pinned model is unavailable with configurable threshold gates (error rate, missing capacity, deprecation flag), and records exact substitution decision in request trace
Shadowed candidate requests populate KV cache and kernel warmness metrics; Console surfaces warmness and divergence signals per-route
Automated rollback triggered if substituted traffic causes >5% absolute increase in error-rate or >30% relative increase in p95 latency over a 5-minute window; manual override available in Console
Playbook and customer notification templates added to Runbook and linked from Console substitution events
implementation_plan: Design scoring proto and add fields to model catalog metadata (compatibility_score, warmness, last_warmed_at, region_affinity)
Add mirror/shadow path in serving runtime that can send copies of in-flight requests to candidate variants with sampling rate configurable per-customer-region
Implement warmness measurement (successful decode rate + KV cache hit pressure + recent token throughput) emitted to metrics and model catalog
Build Rescue Corridor decision engine in router: fallback candidates are ranked by score; gating checks for deprecation flag, capacity, and safety thresholds applied
Add tracing hook to mark substitution decisions and downstream variant used; surface traces in Console and link to Linear ticket when failures spike
E2E tests: unit tests for scoring, chaos tests simulating model retirement and regional capacity loss, perf tests to ensure shadowing overhead <3% p95 impact
Gradual rollout: internal alpha -> canary customers -> 10% opt-in -> default opt-out for pins (announce change)
updates: 2025-02-18: Initial RFC reviewed by Runtime and Platform teams. Feedback: ensure shadowing doesn't double-bill tokens and that privacy is preserved for private deployments.
2025-02-25: Added warmness metric definition and adjusted scoring weights to penalize >20% latency delta more heavily. Requested instrumentation hooks from telemetry team.
2025-03-03: Prototype mirror path implemented (internal build). Observed KV cache warm-up reduces cold p95 by ~18% in microbenchmarks. Need to measure end-to-end cost delta.
2025-03-10: Safety gates refined. Added automated rollback thresholds after incident tabletop with SRE; updated acceptance criteria accordingly. Assigned to Marco for execution.
2025-03-10: Added links to draft runbook and customer-notification templates in links field.
comments: PM review (Jared Lim): Please include a migration communication plan for existing pinned customers — they must opt-in to shadowing by default.
Design review (Rina Soto): Console should indicate when a pin was served from Rescue Corridor and allow one-click pin swap to replacement variant.
SRE (Lina Gomez): Chaos tests must exercise network partitions to validate regional-only rescue behavior and ensure no global spillover.

Security (Owen Park): For Private deployments, shadowing must respect KMS/HSM and not copy plaintext customer data to external model variants. Marked security_review_required=false for now but flagged for implementation checklist.
manual_playbook: Operator step 1: Confirm substitution event in Console -> View traces -> identify substituted variant
Operator step 2: If substitution is degrading, toggle Rescue Corridor to 'pause substitutions' and failover back to global fallback chain
Operator step 3: Notify customers pinned to affected version using template (link in links) and propose replacement pin
Operator step 4: If root cause is capacity, trigger emergency capacity request and engage capacity-on-call
Operator step 5: Postmortem and metrics review within 72 hours; update model catalog compatibility scores based on findings
